meta.title: Dangling Modifier
meta.description: A comprehensive test themed around Indonesian Politics and Government.
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined C1-C2 level grammar structures, primarily featuring Dangling Modifiers paired with other complex topics like passive voice, conditionals, inversion, and relative clauses.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ by the Constitutional Court, the new election law was immediately implemented by the KPU.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect passive participle (avoiding a dangling modifier by correctly modifying 'the new election law') with a passive voice main clause.
explanation.concept: Perfect passive participles correctly modifying the subject of a passive main clause
explanation.formula: Having been + past participle, subject + was/were + past participle
examples: Having been approved by the board, the policy was implemented immediately.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

correctAnswers: While drafting the new omnibus law,

explanation.text: This combines a participle clause with subject-verb agreement. 'Drafting' is a dangling modifier because 'several articles' did not draft the law. Changing it to 'While drafting' creates an elliptical clause, or changing the main subject to 'the government' fixes the dangling modifier. 'Articles' is plural, requiring 'were'.
explanation.concept: Fixing dangling modifiers and ensuring plural agreement
explanation.formula: While + subject + verb-ing, plural subject + were + past participle
examples: While drafting the report, several errors were found.

data.hint: Choose the correct structure to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ effectively, the decentralization policy will empower local governments across the archipelago.

explanation.text: This combines an elliptical conditional clause (avoiding a dangling modifier by implying 'If it is implemented') with the future simple tense.
explanation.concept: Elliptical conditional clauses correctly modifying the main subject
explanation.formula: If + past participle, subject + will + base verb
examples: If handled properly, the crisis will be resolved quickly.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: forced the president to reshuffle the cabinet.

explanation.text: This combines a participle clause with the mandative subjunctive. 'Demanding' is a dangling modifier because a 'scandal' cannot demand; 'the protesters' must be the subject. The subjunctive requires the base form 'resign'.
explanation.concept: Ensuring the modifier's implied subject matches the main clause subject, plus mandative subjunctive
explanation.formula: Demanding that + subject + base verb, plural subject + past simple verb
examples: Demanding that the CEO step down, the shareholders voted against the board.

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ such extensive bureaucratic red tape, rarely have foreign investors felt welcomed in the sector.

explanation.text: This combines a past participle modifier (correctly modifying 'foreign investors') with negative adverbial inversion.
explanation.concept: Past participle modifiers correctly matching the inverted subject
explanation.formula: Past participle + by + noun, rarely + auxiliary + subject + past participle
examples: Overwhelmed by the workload, seldom do employees leave on time.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

correctAnswers: After the committee reviewed the budget proposal,

explanation.text: This combines a prepositional phrase with a gerund (dangling modifier) and subject-verb agreement. The 'allocation of funds' did not review the proposal. The subject must be 'the committee', which takes the singular verb 'approved'.
explanation.concept: Fixing dangling gerund phrases by aligning the subject
explanation.formula: After + subject + verb-ing + object, subject + past simple verb + object
examples: After reviewing the documents, the manager approved the request.

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ more transparently than its predecessor, the current administration has gained significantly higher public trust.

explanation.text: This combines a present participle modifier (correctly modifying 'the current administration') with advanced comparatives.
explanation.concept: Present participle modifiers with comparative structures
explanation.formula: Verb-ing + comparative + than + noun, subject + has/have + past participle
examples: Performing better than the previous model, the new software has received praise.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: Lacking transparency in the procurement process,
correctAnswers: Due to a lack of transparency in the procurement process,
awarded several contracts to affiliated companies.

explanation.text: This combines a participle phrase (dangling modifier) with passive voice. 'Contracts' cannot lack transparency; the 'ministry' does. Changing the modifier to a prepositional phrase or making 'the ministry' the subject fixes the error.
explanation.concept: Converting dangling modifiers to prepositional phrases or active subjects
explanation.formula: Due to + noun phrase, subject + past simple verb + object
examples: Due to heavy rain, the organizers canceled the event.

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ the controversial bill last month, the parliament is now facing intense backlash from labor unions.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect active participle (avoiding a dangling modifier by correctly modifying 'the parliament') with the present continuous tense.
explanation.concept: Perfect active participles indicating an action completed before the main clause
explanation.formula: Having + past participle + object, subject + is/are + verb-ing
examples: Having finished the report, she is now relaxing.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: Looking into the allegations of corruption,
correctAnswers: Looking into the allegations of corruption,

multiErrorSegments.text: by the KPK in the ministry's accounts.

explanation.text: This combines a participle phrase (dangling modifier) with subject-verb agreement. 'Irregularities' did not look into the allegations; 'the KPK' did. 'Found' is the correct active verb.
explanation.concept: Aligning the participle modifier with the correct active subject
explanation.formula: Verb-ing + preposition + object, subject + past simple verb + object
examples: Looking into the issue, the team found several errors.

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ that the infrastructure project was over budget, the auditor general requested a full investigation.

explanation.text: This combines a present participle modifier (correctly modifying 'the auditor general') with a noun clause.
explanation.concept: Present participle modifiers introducing a noun clause
explanation.formula: Verb-ing + that + clause, subject + past simple verb
examples: Realizing that the deadline was near, he worked overtime.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: Representing the interests of the indigenous communities,
correctAnswers: Representing the interests of the indigenous communities,
the activists argued that many of the new policies

explanation.text: This combines a participle phrase (dangling modifier) with quantifiers and subject-verb agreement. 'Policies' do not represent interests; 'activists' do. 'Many of the new policies' is plural, requiring 'ignore'.
explanation.concept: Fixing dangling modifiers and ensuring plural agreement with quantifiers
explanation.formula: Verb-ing + object, subject + verb + that + plural quantifier + plural verb
examples: Representing the workers, the union stated that many of the demands are valid.

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ the historic peace agreement in 2005, it was the former president who facilitated the negotiations in Helsinki.

explanation.text: This combines a perfect active participle (correctly modifying 'the former president' in the cleft sentence) with an it-cleft structure.
explanation.concept: Perfect participle modifiers aligning with the emphasized subject in a cleft sentence
explanation.formula: Having + past participle + object, it was + noun + who + past simple verb
examples: Having designed the prototype, it was the engineer who presented it.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: Seeking an unique solution to the traffic congestion in Jakarta,
correctAnswers: Seeking a unique solution to the traffic congestion in Jakarta,

explanation.text: This combines a participle phrase (dangling modifier) with article usage. 'Policy' cannot seek a solution; 'the governor' can. 'Unique' starts with a consonant sound (/j/), requiring 'a'.
explanation.concept: Fixing dangling modifiers and using correct indefinite articles
explanation.formula: Verb-ing + a + word starting with /j/ sound, subject + past simple verb + object
examples: Seeking a unique approach, the team developed a new strategy.

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ without proper environmental impact assessments, the new mining regulations must have caused significant ecological damage.

explanation.text: This combines a past participle modifier (passive meaning, correctly modifying 'regulations') with a modal verb of deduction in the perfect form.
explanation.topic: Dangling Modifiers + Modal Verbs of Deduction
explanation.concept: Past participle modifiers with passive meaning matching the subject
explanation.formula: Past participle + without + noun, subject + must have + past participle
examples: Released without testing, the software must have contained bugs.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: Although considered a milestone in democratic reforms,
correctAnswers: Although considered a milestone in democratic reforms,

multiErrorSegments.text: by the electoral commission for the new regulations.

explanation.text: This combines an elliptical adverbial clause (dangling modifier) with passive voice. 'Heavy criticism' was not considered a milestone; 'the new electoral regulations' were. The active voice 'faced heavy criticism' resolves the dangling modifier.
explanation.concept: Ensuring the implied subject of an elliptical clause matches the main clause subject
explanation.formula: Although + past participle + object, subject + past simple verb + object
examples: Although praised by critics, the film faced low attendance.

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ by the end of the year, the new capital city of Nusantara will have absorbed billions in state budget allocations.

explanation.text: This combines an elliptical adverbial clause (avoiding a dangling modifier) with the future perfect tense.
explanation.concept: Elliptical clauses correctly modifying the subject of a future perfect main clause
explanation.formula: Once + past participle, subject + will have + past participle
examples: Once finished, the project will have cost millions.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: Serving as the backbone of the nation's agriculture,
correctAnswers: Serving as the backbone of the nation's agriculture,

multiErrorSegments.text: declined significantly over the past decade.

explanation.text: This combines a participle phrase (dangling modifier) with subject-verb agreement. 'The number' does not serve as the backbone; 'farmers' do. 'Farmers' is plural, correctly taking 'have'.
explanation.concept: Aligning participle modifiers with the correct plural subject
explanation.formula: Verb-ing + object, plural subject + have + past participle
examples: Acting as the team's captain, the players have improved their coordination.

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ the widespread public outcry, the government, nevertheless, proceeded with the controversial fuel subsidy reduction.

explanation.text: This combines a present participle modifier (correctly modifying 'the government') with a contrastive discourse marker.
explanation.concept: Present participle modifiers with contrastive discourse markers
explanation.formula: Verb-ing + object, subject, nevertheless, + past simple verb
examples: Despite the warnings, he, however, proceeded with the plan.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: Wishing for a more transparent government,
correctAnswers: Wishing for a more transparent government,
celebrated when the parliament passed the new anti-corruption law

explanation.text: This combines a participle phrase (dangling modifier) with passive voice. A 'law' cannot wish; 'citizens' can. Changing the main clause to an active structure with 'citizens' as the subject fixes the dangling modifier.
explanation.concept: Aligning participle modifiers expressing desire with the correct subject
explanation.formula: Verb-ing + object, subject + past simple verb + object
examples: Hoping for a better outcome, the team practiced harder.

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ the country's economic stability, the minister spoke as though he had complete control over the global market.

explanation.text: This combines a present participle modifier (correctly modifying 'the minister') with an unreal comparison using 'as though'.
explanation.topic: Dangling Modifiers + As Though / As If
explanation.concept: Present participle modifiers with unreal comparisons
explanation.formula: Verb-ing + object, subject + past simple verb + as though + subject + past perfect
examples: Ignoring the risks, he acted as though he had a safety net.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: So complex was the new tax regulation that,

explanation.text: This combines 'so + adjective' inversion with a perfect passive participle (dangling modifier) and subject-verb agreement. 'Loopholes' were not drafted; 'it' (the regulation) was. 'Contained' resolves the dangling modifier.
explanation.concept: Ensuring participle modifiers align with the subject in inverted structures
explanation.formula: So + adjective + be + subject + that, having been + past participle, it + past simple verb + object
examples: So difficult was the test that, having been designed poorly, it confused the students.

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ the necessary parliamentary approval, the decree would have been struck down by the Constitutional Court.

explanation.text: This combines a present participle modifier (correctly modifying 'the decree') with third conditional inversion.
explanation.concept: Present participle modifiers matching the subject of an inverted conditional
explanation.formula: Verb-ing + object, subject + would have + past participle
examples: Missing the deadline, the application would have been rejected.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: Not only did the policy fail to reduce poverty,
but having been implemented without proper funding,
correctAnswers: but having been implemented without proper funding,

explanation.text: This combines 'not only... but also' inversion with a perfect passive participle (dangling modifier). 'Communities' did not implement the policy; 'it' (the policy) did. Restructuring the main clause fixes the dangling modifier.
explanation.topic: Dangling Modifiers + Not Only ... But Also
explanation.concept: Aligning participle modifiers with the correct subject in correlative conjunctions
explanation.formula: Not only + auxiliary + subject + verb, but having been + past participle, it + past simple verb + object + to-infinitive
examples: Not only did the plan fail, but having been rushed, it caused the team to panic.

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ the depths of the political scandal, little did the newly appointed minister know that his career was about to end.

explanation.text: This combines an adjective phrase (correctly modifying 'the newly appointed minister') with negative adverbial inversion.
explanation.topic: Dangling Modifiers + Little Did He Know
explanation.concept: Adjective phrases correctly modifying the subject of an inverted clause
explanation.formula: Adjective + preposition + object, little + auxiliary + subject + base verb
examples: Oblivious to the danger, little did he know what was coming.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: Under no circumstances should the classified documents be leaked,
correctAnswers: Under no circumstances should the intelligence agency leak the classified documents,

explanation.text: This combines negative adverbial inversion with a perfect active participle (dangling modifier). The 'documents' did not mark themselves; 'the intelligence agency' did. Making 'the intelligence agency' the subject of the main clause fixes the dangling modifier.
explanation.concept: Aligning participle modifiers with the subject in negative inversion
explanation.formula: Under no circumstances + auxiliary + subject + base verb + object, having + past participle + object
examples: Under no circumstances should you share the password, having promised to keep it secret.

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ any clarification regarding the new voting procedures, the public is advised to contact the election officials.

explanation.text: This combines a present participle modifier (correctly modifying 'the public') with a formal conditional structure in the main clause.
explanation.concept: Present participle modifiers implying a condition for the main subject
explanation.formula: Verb-ing + object, subject + is/are + advised + to-infinitive
examples: Requiring assistance, the patient is advised to call the nurse.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: Were I to become the president,

correctAnswers: I would reallocate the national budget

explanation.text: This combines second conditional inversion with a present participle (dangling modifier). The 'national budget' does not prioritize reform; 'I' do. Changing the main clause subject to 'I' and using 'would reallocate' fixes the dangling modifier and conditional mismatch.
explanation.concept: Aligning participle modifiers with the subject in inverted conditionals
explanation.formula: Were + subject + to + base verb, verb-ing + object, subject + would + base verb + object
examples: Were I to lead the project, focusing on quality, I would allocate more resources.

data.hint: Choose the correct modifier to complete the sentence.
data.question: _____ by a special committee, the proposed amendment, which aims to strengthen judicial independence, is currently under review.

explanation.text: This combines a past participle modifier (passive meaning, correctly modifying 'the proposed amendment') with a non-defining relative clause.
explanation.topic: Dangling Modifiers + Advanced Passive + Relative Clause
explanation.concept: Past participle modifiers with passive meaning matching the subject of a relative clause
explanation.formula: Past participle + by + agent, subject, which + verb + s/es + object, + is/are + preposition + noun
examples: Written by an expert, the report, which details the findings, is ready.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

multiErrorSegments.text: Had the coalition not collapsed last year,

correctAnswers: the government's implementation of the new infrastructure plan

explanation.text: This combines third conditional inversion with a present participle (dangling modifier) and a mixed conditional main clause. The 'economy' did not implement the plan; 'the government's implementation' did. Restructuring the subject fixes the dangling modifier.
explanation.concept: Aligning participle modifiers with the correct subject in mixed conditionals
explanation.formula: Had + subject + not + past participle, subject's + verb-ing + of + object + would + be + adjective
examples: Had the team not disbanded, their execution of the strategy would be successful today.
